A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present embeddings with a balanced l/i and l/i /l load for a complete binary tree architecture T and a complete binary tree or a hypercube architecture H.

we show how to embed a complete binary tree into a complete binary tree of smaller size with a balanced load, and that this problem can be solved in a way that achieves a balanced load, a small dilation, and a small congestion.
we present embeddings for T with dilation 1, congestion min{[ n/m ], 2log n } and balanced load, and embeddings with dilation 2[loglog m ] + 2, congestion O(log n ) and balanced l/i load.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the load of a tree embedding can be made balanced with a small dilation and a small congestion, and that a balanced l/i processor load can be achieved by an embedding with a small dilation, but the congestion is high.
the problem of embedding complete binary trees with a balanced processor load can be reduced to the problem of embedding a single binary tree with the same number of leaves and interior nodes.
the load balancing problem for embeddings can be reduced to a problem in graph theory.
